evidence.claim: The U.S. Census Bureau reported Q1 2026 adjusted retail ecommerce sales of $326.7 billion, up 2.7% from Q4 2025 and up 9.8% year over year; ecommerce accounted for 16.9% of total retail sales.
evidence.source_title: Monthly Retail Trade - Quarterly Retail E-Commerce Sales Report

evidence.claim: NRF and Happy Returns projected 2025 U.S. retail merchandise returns of $849.9 billion, online returns at 19.3% of online sales, and return fraud at 9% of returns.
UPS announced in October 2023 that it would acquire Happy Returns, a software and reverse-logistics company enabling box-free, no-label returns for merchants and consumers.
evidence.source_title: UPS to Acquire Happy Returns, a Leader in Reverse Logistics

evidence.claim: UPS's Happy Returns page describes a returns-management solution with drop-off at Return Bars or UPS Stores, verified returns, shipment consolidation, and fraud monitoring across the Return Bar network.
evidence.source_title: Ecommerce Returns Management with Happy Returns | UPS

evidence.claim: WEX's 2025 annual report describes corporate payments capabilities including virtual card products, automated reporting/reconciliation, ERP integrations, supplier data analysis, and embedded payments focused on areas including travel.

Shift4 completed its acquisition of Global Blue in 2025, adding a technology platform for tax-free shopping, dynamic currency conversion, and payment solutions used by premium retail and hospitality locations serving international travelers.
evidence.source_title: Shift4 Completes Acquisition of Global Blue

evidence.claim: Frontdoor's 2025 annual report states that its preferred contractor network completed approximately 84% of home warranty service requests in 2025 and that it operates in a U.S. home services industry estimated at more than $500 billion of annual revenue.
Frontdoor describes itself as the largest U.S. provider of home service plans, with approximately 17,000 pre-qualified professional contractor firms and more than 2.2 million customers nationwide.

Central Garden & Pet's 2025 annual-report disclosure says it is a manufacturer and distributor of branded and private-label products for U.S. lawn & garden and pet supplies markets; Walmart, Home Depot, Lowe's, Costco, and Amazon together accounted for about 54% of fiscal 2025 net sales.
evidence.source_title: Central Garden & Pet Company 2025 Annual Report

evidence.claim: ReposiTrak's 2025 10-K describes a SaaS B2B ecommerce, compliance, traceability, and supply-chain management platform serving retailers, wholesalers, distributors, and suppliers; its Traceability Network connects supplier locations to food wholesaler and retail locations.
Assurant reported that U.S. consumers received more than $6.4 billion in value through mobile trade-in programs in 2025, up 42% year over year.
evidence.source_title: Assurant Reports Record $6.4 Billion Returned to Consumers Through Device Innovation and Trade-In Programs in 2025

evidence.claim: Assurant's 2025 annual-report material describes mobile business offerings including end-to-end mobile device lifecycle solutions, trade-in and upgrade, and asset-value recovery.

Flywire acquired Sertifi in February 2025 to accelerate its travel business; Sertifi digitizes hospitality-specific workflows and payments, integrates with property and catering systems, and supports more than 20,000 hotel locations globally.
evidence.source_title: Flywire Acquires Sertifi to Accelerate Travel Business and Expand Offering to Support Over 20,000 Hotel Locations Globally

evidence.claim: Flywire's 2025 annual-report filing states that Sertifi was intended to accelerate the travel business and expand offerings to support over 20,000 hotel locations globally.
Graphic Packaging describes its business as sustainable paperboard packaging and recyclable folding cartons across food, beverage, and consumer-goods markets.

memory_update.text: UPS is a reference anchor for ecommerce returns convenience and consolidation because Happy Returns combines returns portal software, item verification, drop-off network, fraud monitoring, and UPS parcel infrastructure.

WEX should remain in the underfollowed lane for travel payments only if Corporate Payments disclosures show material travel or embedded-payments growth; otherwise it risks being mostly fleet/benefits exposure.
Shift4's Global Blue acquisition gives FOUR a clearer cross-border travel-retail infrastructure relationship than a generic merchant acquirer label suggests.
Frontdoor maps to the consumer home-repair contractor-capacity node through its contractor network and home-service-plan fulfillment, not just warranty/insurance classification.

Central Garden & Pet has a potentially important retailer-dependency/private-label relationship because it manufactures and distributes branded and private-label pet/garden products and has meaningful concentration to large retailers.

ReposiTrak is a speculative shadow candidate for grocery traceability and retail supplier connectivity; survival to later layers requires proof of retailer-mandated supplier onboarding and scalable recurring SaaS economics.
Assurant's mobile device lifecycle and trade-in programs create a reverse-logistics/recommerce relationship hidden inside an insurance/protection-plan classification.
Flywire's Sertifi acquisition creates a travel/hospitality payments and property-system workflow relationship that may be obscured by Flywire's education and healthcare vertical payments framing.
Graphic Packaging is a reference packaging node for private-label and shelf-ready consumer packaging conversion, but evidence is currently more generic than ticker-specific to private-label growth.
Need current market caps, analyst coverage counts, liquidity, and revenue purity for WEX, FOUR, FTDR, CENTA, TRAK, AIZ, FLYW, GPK, and UPS before Layer 2C prioritization.
Need direct customer evidence tying candidates to Walmart, Amazon, Target, Costco, Home Depot, Lowe's, Booking, Expedia, major grocers, telecom carriers, OEMs, hotel chains, or OTAs.

Need falsification metrics per node: returns cost not improving, travel payment volume not material, contractor completion rates deteriorating, retailer insourcing, private-label mix stagnating, FSMA deadline delays, device resale ASP pressure, or packaging volume declines.

summary: Mapped the visible candidate chunk across consumer infrastructure nodes: ecommerce returns/reverse logistics, travel and hospitality payments rails, home-repair fulfillment networks, private-label/retail supplier dependency, food traceability SaaS, device lifecycle/recommerce, and packaging. The strongest reference anchors are UPS/Happy Returns and Graphic Packaging. The highest underfollowed relationship candidates for later verification are WEX, Frontdoor, ReposiTrak, Assurant, Flywire, Central Garden & Pet, and Shift4. No buy/sell view is expressed; this is a relationship map for follow-up evidence collection.

ticker_relationships.hidden_signal_to_verify: Adoption of Happy Returns by enterprise merchants, economics of item-level scanning and consolidation, franchise-store incentives, and whether portal-agnostic returns increase UPS parcel share.
ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Track UPS disclosures on Happy Returns merchant count, return-location count, package consolidation economics, returns-related revenue, store/franchise compensation, and fraud-reduction metrics.
ticker_relationships.node: Ecommerce returns, reverse logistics, return drop-off network, and returns-routing software
ticker_relationships.relationship: Reference leader for scaled box-free/no-label returns infrastructure. UPS's Happy Returns provides a merchant returns portal, item verification/scanning, drop-off locations, consolidation, and parcel-network integration; this sets the operating benchmark for smaller reverse-logistics and returns-software candidates.

ticker_relationships.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether travel-related corporate payments volume is growing faster than the rest of WEX, and whether fraud reduction, supplier acceptance, chargeback controls, and reconciliation complexity create durable pricing power.
ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Pull WEX 2025 10-K and Q1/Q2 2026 calls for Corporate Payments purchase volume, travel customer examples, take-rate, supplier acceptance, virtual-card penetration, cross-border mix, and loss/fraud commentary.
ticker_relationships.node: Travel distribution middleware, corporate travel payments, virtual cards, supplier settlement, fraud controls, and reconciliation
ticker_relationships.relationship: Underfollowed payments-rail exposure: WEX is usually framed around fleet/fuel and corporate payments, but its corporate/embedded payments capabilities map to travel intermediaries that need virtual-card issuance, authorization, supplier settlement, reporting, and reconciliation workflows.

ticker_relationships.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether travel/hospitality volume and Global Blue’s cross-border services materially move net revenue, gross profit, and take-rate versus being diluted by broader merchant acquiring exposure.
ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Track 2026 segment commentary for Global Blue revenue contribution, DCC/tax-free-shopping transaction volumes, merchant-location expansion, hospitality payment volume, integration costs, and cross-selling into Shift4 merchants.
ticker_relationships.node: Hospitality, travel retail, cross-border payments, dynamic currency conversion, tax-free shopping, and merchant acquiring
ticker_relationships.relationship: Second-order travel and hospitality infrastructure exposure. Shift4's Global Blue acquisition added tax-free shopping, dynamic currency conversion, and cross-border retail/hospitality technology used by premium merchants serving international travelers.

ticker_relationships.hidden_signal_to_verify: Contractor availability, service-request completion rates, cost inflation in HVAC/plumbing/electrical trades, customer retention, and whether non-warranty home services scale beyond the warranty base.
ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Verify 2026 quarterly disclosures for service-request volume, preferred-contractor completion rate, claims cost inflation, HVAC upgrade adoption, renewal rate, customer count, and gross margin impact from labor/parts inflation.
ticker_relationships.node: Housing repair/remodel contractor supply, home-service plans, HVAC/plumbing/electrical/appliance repair coordination

Frontdoor monetizes nondiscretionary home breakdowns through home service plans and a preferred contractor network; this maps to the contractor-capacity and repair-versus-new-construction node rather than only warranty/insurance classification.

ticker_relationships.hidden_signal_to_verify: Share of revenue from private-label products, Walmart/Target/Home Depot/Lowe's exposure, margin difference between branded and private-label SKUs, dependence on exclusive active ingredient supply, and capacity constraints in pet consumables or garden chemicals.

Central Garden & Pet manufactures and distributes branded and private-label pet and lawn/garden products, with meaningful sales concentration to large retailers; this creates a possible second-order path from retailer private-label/value initiatives and shelf-space allocation.

ticker_relationships.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether retailer mandates pull thousands of suppliers onto the network at low acquisition cost, and whether subscription revenue scales without bespoke implementation costs.
ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Verify customer mandates, supplier-location additions, recurring revenue growth, churn, gross margin, implementation cost, FSMA 204 deadline impact, and whether the FDA compliance extension slows near-term adoption.
